title: AI Control System for Fusion Energy
summary: Next Step Fusion reports that reinforcement learning controlled plasma parameters at DIII-D during 2023–24 and improved controller training. Energy benefits remain future-facing.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Next Step Fusion reports that reinforcement learning controlled plasma parameters at DIII-D during 2023–24 and improved controller training. Energy benefits remain future-facing. Research / fusion-control trials. The chapter reports the stated benefit but does not independently verify it.
purpose: Improve plasma control for fusion research and future reactors.
system: Next Step Fusion reinforcement-learning plasma controller
deployer: DIII-D National Fusion Facility research program

ratings.reason: The source reports experimental plasma-parameter control at DIII-D and more efficient controller training. This is a demonstrated research capability, not commercial fusion output.
Reliable clean energy remains a future application; delivered energy and climate benefits are unknown.

ai_role.statement: A reinforcement-learning policy controls plasma parameters from sensor and actuator data, reducing dependence on intermediate reconstructions in the experimental controller.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 13: AI Control System for Fusion Energy

produced_by: Causal conditions are not established separately in the extracted chapter.
must_hold: Control evaluation within a fusion research facility

headline: Reinforcement learning controls fusion plasma

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
